questions.problem: Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{49}∼N(-7,{14}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $n=49$ from a normal population, what is the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}?$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
n=49,\,\mu =-7,\,\sigma =14.
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(-7,\frac{{14}^{2}}{49}) \\  & ∼N(-7,4).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(7,\frac{{14}^{2}}{49}) \\  & ∼N(7,4).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(6.8<\overset{―}{X}<7.5).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(6.8<\overset{―}{X}<7.5) & =P(\frac{6.8-7}{\sqrt{4}}<Z<\frac{7.5-7}{\sqrt{4}}) \\  & =P(-0.1<Z<0.25) \\  & =Φ(0.25)-Φ(-0.1)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.25)=0.5987,\end{aligned}
$$

and by the symmetry of the normal distribution,

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.1) & =1-Φ(0.1) \\  & =1-0.5398 \\  & =0.4602.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(6.8<\overset{―}{X}<7.5) & =Φ(0.25)-Φ(-0.1) \\  & =0.5987-0.4602 \\  & =0.1385.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The concentration of solute of a certain chemical solution is normally distributed with a mean of $20\,\text{mg/ml}$ and a standard deviation of $1\,\text{mg/ml}.$ Suppose $50$ bottles of this solution are randomly selected. What is the probability that the mean concentration for this sample will be more than $19.9\,\text{mg/ml},$ but less than $20.1\,\text{mg/ml}?$ *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.7\,$ $\,0.2420\,$ $\,0.2389\,$ $\,0.2358\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2743\,$ $\,0.2709\,$ $\,0.2676\,$
$\,-0.5\,$ $\,0.3085\,$ $\,0.3050\,$ $\,0.3015\,$

$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,0.5\,$ $\,0.6915\,$ $\,0.6950\,$ $\,0.6985\,$
$\,0.6\,$ $\,0.7257\,$ $\,0.7291\,$ $\,0.7324\,$
$\,0.7\,$ $\,0.7580\,$ $\,0.7611\,$ $\,0.7642\,$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

 then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

We're told that the population mean $\mu =20,$ the population standard deviation $\sigma =1,$ and that the sample size $n=50.$ Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(20,\frac{{1}^{2}}{50}) \\  & ∼N(20,0.02).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(19.9<\overset{―}{X}<20.1).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(19.9<\overset{―}{X}<20.1) & =P(\frac{19.9-20}{\sqrt{0.02}}<Z<\frac{20.1-20}{\sqrt{0.02}}) \\  & =P(-0.71<Z<0.71) \\  & =Φ(0.71)-Φ(-0.71)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.71) & =0.2389 \\ Φ(0.71) & =0.7611.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(19.9<\overset{―}{X}<20.1) & =Φ(0.71)-Φ(-0.71) \\  & ≈0.7611-0.2389 \\  & =0.5222.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

 then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

We're told that the population mean $\mu =15,$ the population standard deviation $\sigma =2,$ and that the sample size $n=16.$ Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(15,\frac{{2}^{2}}{16}) \\  & ∼N(15,0.25).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(14.7<\overset{―}{X}<15.3).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(14.7<\overset{―}{X}<15.3) & =P(\frac{14.7-15}{\sqrt{0.25}}<Z<\frac{15.3-15}{\sqrt{0.25}}) \\  & =P(-0.6<Z<0.6) \\  & =Φ(0.6)-Φ(-0.6)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.6) & ≈0.7257 \\ Φ(-0.6) & ≈0.2743.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(14.7<\overset{―}{X}<15.3) & =Φ(0.6)-Φ(-0.6) \\  & ≈0.7257-0.2743 \\  & =0.4514.\end{aligned}
$$
